pull.title: Add output script index and corresponding script history RPC
pull.body:
Add a new index `txoscriptindex` which indexes all output scripts. Introduce a new `getscripthistory` RPC that returns all transactions that create outputs corresponding to the provided scripts, and optionally the transactions that spend those outputs if `txospenderindex` is also configured.

This has been a long-requested feature, attempted in previous PRs (#2802, #3652, #6835, #10370, #14053).
Some concerns raised were about the ability for an index like this to scale. I think the new techniques being used to build the indexes (https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35531, https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36002) alleviate this concern. This index can be synced in a few hours and the current disk usage is ~52 GB. This is less than the ~66 GB `txindex` disk usage in v31 and earlier. This index can also be used with a pruned node, so a full node can be supported in < 100 GB of disk space. Missing blocks are returned by hash and can be requested from peers using `getblockfrompeer`.

Some other previous concerns were more conceptual, that this type of index could encourage address reuse and chain analysis. IMO this ship has sailed, and the current status quo of not shipping an address index is turning off users who expect this functionality. Workarounds involve installing, configuring, and syncing other third-party software, making the UX of using Bitcoin Core in a self-sovereign way unnecessarily difficult.

The index hashes each output script with SHA256, then applies salted SipHash-1-3-UJ and stores a five-byte prefix. This is to support the popular Electrum protocol, which supplies only the script hash. The RPC can also look up by address or descriptors. Ranged descriptors are also supported, so a single RPC call can return the entire history of a receive/change xpub pair.

Because there are some scripts with millions of outputs, we introduce a new `OrderedVarInt` which serializes the block height after the script hash prefix. This lets LevelDB seek directly to the prefix + block height, so we can page by block height range.

To prevent DoS concerns by supplying an address with millions of outputs, the RPC tracks a byte budget of reads and throws immediately if too many reads are attempted. The error message instructs the user to narrow the block range.

Improvements to `txospenderindex` (https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36480) will also allow us to use that pruned. The end result would allow users to run with all optional indexes (including this one) in < 200 GB of disk space. Of course a larger pruned setting would be desired if many historical block lookups were being requested.

Concept ACK.

Reviewed 614302e7d14a16fe28a2e8945fa99165693fcf94. I built it and ran `txoscriptindex_tests`, `baseindex_tests`, `rpc_getscripthistory.py`, `rpc_misc.py`, `feature_init.py` and `feature_assumeutxo.py`, all passing. I also did a manual regtest run: address, Electrum scripthash, ranged `wpkh()` descriptor, verbosity 0/1/2, and spender linking. Results matched expectations. My comments are mostly about structure:

**1. The lookup budget does not count block and undo reads.** At verbosity 2, `tx_to_json` reads the full block and its undo data for every block that holds a non-coinbase match (`rpc/blockchain.cpp:4116`). Step 10 also reads a full block whenever two or more extra spenders share one (`rpc/blockchain.cpp:4064`). Neither read is charged. I ran this on regtest with 150 matches, each in its own block padded to ~60 kB. Bytes read by bitcoind during one call (`rchar`):

| verbosity | matching tx bytes | bytes read by node |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | 52,039 | 0.94 MB |
| 2 | 52,039 | 21.2 MB |

On mainnet that means one full block plus its undo data per matching block. A query that fits in the 50 MiB budget can therefore read far more than 50 MiB. Either charge these reads, or say in the help text that the budget does not cover them.

**2. `OrderedVarInt` could be `BigEndianFormatter<3>`.** Big-endian already sorts by height, and the same key already uses it for the tx offset. Both encodings are 3 bytes for heights 16,512 through 2,113,663 (roughly until 2048). After that, BE3 stays at 3 bytes while `OrderedVarInt` grows to 4, and BE3 goes up to height 16,777,215. I tried it locally. It removes `ordered_varint.h` and its tests (+4/−210), and the PR's unit and functional tests still pass:

```diff
+    static constexpr uint32_t HEIGHT_SIZE{3};
 ...
-                  Using<OrderedVarIntFormatter>(obj.height),
+                  Using<BigEndianFormatter<HEIGHT_SIZE>>(obj.height),
```

**3. Ordering spenders doesn't need a block read.** `txospenderindex` keys already store a `CDiskTxPos`, and its `nTxOffset` grows with the transaction's position in the block. I added it to `TxoSpender` and sorted extra spenders by `(height, tx_offset)`. That removes the grouping loop and the `GetBlockChecked` call (+6/−20). `test_confirmed_transaction_order` still passes. It fails if the offset is dropped from the comparison, so the test does cover this.

**4. `Find` could take the whole set of script hashes.** Today the RPC calls `Find` once per hash and merges results by `(height, tx_offset)`. A transaction paying two scripts of one descriptor is read and charged twice; `rpc_getscripthistory.py` relies on this ("repeated reads of overlapping transactions exceed the work budget"). A multi-hash `Find` would read each candidate once and drop both `ScriptHistoryMatch::tx_offset` and the `by_position` merge. The budget would then trip later than it does now, never earlier, so that test case would need updating. Returning pruned blocks as their own set instead of null-`tx` placeholders would also remove the duplicated branch at `index/txoscriptindex.cpp:163` and `:174`, and the matching filter in the RPC.

**5. One budget, one error.** Index lookups charge a `uint64_t&` and fail with "Script history index lookup limit exceeded…". Extra transaction bodies throw a `std::runtime_error` with "Script history exceeds the … byte budget" (`rpc/blockchain.cpp:3933`). Both enforce the same limit through two code paths with two messages. The index-layer message also names RPC options (`index/txoscriptindex.cpp:138`). A small budget type that both layers charge, with the user-facing wording kept in the RPC, would be simpler.

**6. Could the RPC go in its own file?** `blockchain.cpp` grows by ~530 lines to 4,238. The handler is one ~400-line lambda that opens with a 12-step index comment. `src/rpc/scripthistory.cpp` with one function per step would be easier to read and review.

**7. `TxToJSON` is now declared in `rawtransaction_util.h`.** That header belongs to `bitcoin_common`, which the wallet also links. `TxToJSON` takes a `Chainstate` and is still defined in `rawtransaction.cpp` in `bitcoin_node`. Declaring it in a node-side header would keep that boundary clean.

Nits:
- The mempool scan matches against `scripts` or `script_hashes` depending on how the query was given (`rpc/blockchain.cpp:3986`). Hashing everything up front would leave one set and remove the branch.
- When `range` is given, the descriptor is parsed twice: once at `rpc/blockchain.cpp:3896` and again inside `EvalDescriptorStringOrObject`.
- `RawTransactionDoc` changes the `getrawtransaction` help text:
  - `blockhash` moves below `vsize_adjusted` and gains "(omitted for mempool transactions)".
  - The `hex` description changes.
  - At verbosity 2, `fee` moves to the end.

  Probably fine, but worth a line in the commit message.

---

comments.body:
> SHA256(scriptPubKey)

Electrum 1.7.x protocol is now using [scriptPubKey-based subscription and queries](https://electrum-protocol.readthedocs.io/en/latest/protocol-changes.html#version-1-7), so maybe it would simpler to avoid SHA256 here?
